findings.basisJa: WEB 25:5 says Amaziah “gathered Judah together” and then “all Judah and Benjamin”; this denotes a people/army, not the region alone. The row maps Benjamin but omits Judah and has no unresolved-candidate record for Judah. Add a collective disposition or explicitly record that no compatible Judah-people ID is confirmed; do not substitute place:judah_1280.

WEB 25:23 names “gate of Ephraim” as a gate in Jerusalem. place:gate_of_ephraim_402 is mapped, but person:ephraim_1206 is also added as context even though the verse does not mention the Ephraimite people or tribe. Remove that lineage link; the gate name alone is not a collective reference.

WEB 26:1 explicitly says “All the people of Judah” made Uzziah king. Judah’s collective use is absent and no unresolved-candidate row records it. The nearby place:judah_1280 must not stand in for the people; record the missing/held group explicitly.

WEB 28:6 says Pekah killed 120,000 “in Judah.” The row maps the two kings but omits the named territory place:judah_1280, although the sentence locates the deaths there. Add the geographic referent; distinguish it from Judah’s people.

WEB 29:17 continues the cleansing narrative (“they began…they came…they sanctified”) immediately after the priests/Levites in 29:16. The row maps only God, with no actor context or unresolved actor note. At minimum record the clear priest/Levite continuity using the appropriate group relation; do not silently omit it.

WEB 29:18 says “they went in to Hezekiah… and said”; the agents are the priests/Levites just named in 29:16–17. Hezekiah is mapped, but the explicit reporting group is missing and no unresolved note explains it.

WEB 29:21 names “Judah” as one of the offering’s beneficiaries (“for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah”). The row maps Aaron and God but omits the Judah polity/region and has no unresolved record. Add place:judah_1280 if interpreting the territory, or explicitly hold the referent.

WEB 30:5 uses Dan in the geographic range “from Beersheba even to Dan.” place:dan_323 is appropriate, but person:dan_973 is the ancestor/tribal person and is not named as an actor or collective here. Remove the person link.

WEB 30:6 says “the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel”; this is the patriarch Israel/Jacob, not the Israelite collective person:israel_682. Replace with the existing person:jacob_683 (or record an unresolved textual-identity hold if the map’s book-local policy prevents it); do not map the nation as a patriarch.

WEB 30:10 explicitly says “through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh, even to Zebulun.” The row links person:ephraim_1206, person:manasseh_1928, and person:zebulun_3002, treating named tribal territories as ancestors/people. Territory IDs exist for Ephraim (place:ephraim_401 / ephraim-territory_1292), Zebulun (place:zebulun_1289), and Manasseh’s halves (1290/1291); use the supported territory or leave the imprecise Manasseh extent unresolved.

WEB 31:1 distinguishes “cities of Judah” from the further locations “in Ephraim and Manasseh.” The row maps the latter two only as person/tribal IDs, even though the phrase is geographic; a territory ID exists for Ephraim and east/west territory IDs for Manasseh. Do not present the ancestor IDs as the places. Also record the separate “all Judah” collective if no group ID is available.
WEB 31:4 explicitly locates the residents in Jerusalem. The row has Hezekiah and Levi but omits place:jerusalem_636, with no exclusion or unresolved reason.

WEB 32:9 explicitly says Sennacherib sent servants “to Jerusalem, to Hezekiah king of Judah, and to all Judah who were at Jerusalem.” The row has Sennacherib/Assyria/Lachish only; it omits direct place Jerusalem, person Hezekiah, and the Judah collective/held disposition. These are not inferable from the map’s other chapter rows.
WEB 32:10 explicitly names Jerusalem (“remain under siege in Jerusalem”). The row maps Sennacherib and Assyria only, omitting place:jerusalem_636.

WEB 32:12 names both Judah and Jerusalem in Sennacherib’s speech (“commanded Judah and Jerusalem”). The row maps Hezekiah only. Add the place/polity Jerusalem and an appropriately distinguished Judah referent or an explicit unresolved collective; do not silently omit the named terms.

WEB 32:18 says the servants called out to “the people of Jerusalem who were on the wall.” The row maps only Sennacherib; place:jerusalem_636 (and the relevant inhabitants if a canonical collective is available) is omitted.

WEB 33:9 says Manasseh seduced “Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.” The row maps Manasseh, God, Israel, and Jerusalem, but neither the Judah collective nor an unresolved Judah disposition; it does not establish that the region ID alone is the people.
WEB 33:16 explicitly says Manasseh “commanded Judah to serve the LORD.” The row maps Manasseh, God, and Israel, but omits Judah and gives no unresolved collective record.

WEB 34:6 says Josiah acted “in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, even to Naphtali.” This is a geographic list of tribal territories, not the patriarchs’ actions. The row maps four person IDs (Ephraim, Manasseh, Simeon, Naphtali); use compatible place territories where available and explicitly hold the others/extent.

WEB 34:9 names the contributors “Manasseh, Ephraim, … all Judah and Benjamin” (with Israel’s remnant and Jerusalem’s inhabitants). Judah is absent from the row and no unresolved collective entry is recorded. Do not let the Jerusalem place or other tribal person IDs stand in for Judah’s people.

WEB 34:21 requests inquiry for “those who are left in Israel and in Judah.” The row maps Israel but omits Judah and does not record an unresolved Judah collective; the two populations are explicitly paired.

WEB 34:23 opens Huldah’s message with “The LORD, the God of Israel says.” The row links God and Huldah but omits the explicit Israel relation that the map records in comparable “God of Israel” formulations elsewhere. Add person:israel_682 as contextual collective relation, not as the patriarch or territory.

WEB 34:26 directly addresses “the king of Judah.” The row maps God and Josiah but omits the named Judah polity/territory, although place:judah_1280 is used for the same royal-territory sense elsewhere. Add it or record a precise unresolved reason.

WEB 34:29 says the king gathered “all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem”; Jerusalem is mapped but Judah’s people/polity is not. A collective Judah ID is not established by the map, so this omission must remain unresolved rather than be treated as complete.

WEB 35:18 explicitly includes “all Judah and Israel who were present.” Israel is mapped; Judah is correctly kept separate from its region and is listed as unresolved-canonical-candidate. Source choice is safe but the row is not complete/runtime-ready.

WEB 36:4 says Eliakim was made king “over Judah and Jerusalem.” Jerusalem is mapped but Judah is omitted, with no unresolved note. The political/territorial referent must be represented separately from a people ID.
WEB 36:10 says Zedekiah was made king “over Judah and Jerusalem.” The row maps the kings and Jerusalem but omits the explicit Judah polity/territory and does not record an unresolved disposition.

WEB 36:17 names the “king of the Chaldeans,” while the row maps God but leaves the king/army unresolved. The preceding chapter events name Nebuchadnezzar, but the verse’s compressed retrospective does not identify the king by name; retain as a qualified unresolved candidate until explicit source-context identification is accepted.

WEB 29:22 explicitly says “the priests received the blood” and repeatedly describes them killing/sprinkling the offerings. This row is empty even though 29:21 identifies the priests as the sons of Aaron, and the map has an Aaron ID for that lineage. Add a supported Aaronic-priest context relation or explicitly record the priest collective as unresolved.

WEB 29:23 says “They brought near” the male goats immediately after 29:22’s named priests; likely priestly actors, but the verse does not repeat their name. The empty row has no explicit context/unresolved note. Keep qualified pending a justified Aaronic-priest context or an unresolved actor entry.
